**Eden Michael Walter Hazard** (born 7 January 1991) is a Belgian professional [footballer](Association_football "Association football") who plays as a [winger](Winger_(association_football) "Winger (association football)") or [attacking midfielder](Attacking_midfielder "Attacking midfielder"). Known for his creativity, [dribbling](Dribbling "Dribbling"), passing and vision, Hazard is considered one of the best players of his generation.[[2]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-2)

Hazard began his senior career with [Ligue 1](Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") club [Lille](Lille_OSC "Lille OSC") in 2007 at the age of 16 and soon became an integral part of the Lille team under manager [Rudi Garcia](Rudi_Garcia "Rudi Garcia"). In his first full season, he became the first non-French player to win the [Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year](Ligue_1_Young_Player_of_the_Year "Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year") award, and the following season became the first player to win the award twice. After making over 190 appearances and scoring 50 goals for Lille, Hazard signed for English club [Chelsea](Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") in June 2012. Hazard made his amateur debut on 1 September 2007 in a league match against [Racing Club de France](Racing_Levallois_92 "Racing Levallois 92"). appearing as a second-half [substitute](Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") in a 3–1 defeat.[[17]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-17) He made his first start a week later in the team's 1–0 defeat to [Lesquin](US_Lesquin "US Lesquin").[[18]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-18)

After spending the majority of October and the early part of November playing with the club's under-18 team, on 14 November, due to several players being on international duty, Hazard was called up to the senior team by manager [Claude Puel](Claude_Puel "Claude Puel") to participate in a [friendly](Friendly_(association_football) "Friendly (association football)") against Belgian club [Club Brugge](Club_Brugge_KV "Club Brugge KV") on 16 November.[[19]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-19) He appeared as a substitute in the match and, as a result of his performance, was included in the 18-man squad to face [Nancy](AS_Nancy_Lorraine "AS Nancy Lorraine") in a league match on 24 November,[[20]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-20) where he subsequently made his professional debut in the match, coming on as a substitute in the 78th minute.[[21]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-21)

Hazard returned to the club's reserve team and spent December playing with the squad. Following the winter break, Hazard returned to the first team in January and made substitute appearances in three league matches against [Metz](FC_Metz "FC Metz"), [Sochaux](FC_Sochaux-Montb%C3%A9liard "FC Sochaux-Montbéliard"), and [Paris Saint-Germain](Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint-Germain F.C.").[[22]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-22)[[23]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-23)[[24]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-24) Following the match against PSG, he was demoted back to amateur level where he played concurrently with the reserve team in the fourth division and the under-18 team in the Coupe Gambardella. On 17 May 2008, he scored his first amateur goal in a 3–2 victory over [Vitré](AS_Vitr%C3%A9 "AS Vitré").[[25]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-25) Hazard finished his amateur career with 11 appearances and one goal, helping the reserve team finished in fifth place, which was first among professional clubs' reserve teams playing in the group.[[26]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-26)[[27]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-27)

#### 2008–2010: Debut season and individual success

Hazard was promoted to the firstm team permanently by new manager [Rudi Garcia](Rudi_Garcia "Rudi Garcia") ahead of the [2008–09 season](2008%E2%80%9309_Ligue_1 "2008–09 Ligue 1"). Early on, he made substitute appearances regularly, including against [Auxerre](AJ_Auxerre "AJ Auxerre") on 20 September, when he scored a goal to make it 2–2 in the 88th minute in a game Lille won 3–2 in [stoppage time](Stoppage_time "Stoppage time") following a goal from [Túlio de Melo](T%C3%BAlio_de_Melo "Túlio de Melo").[[28]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-28) Hazard's first career goal resulted in him becoming the youngest goalscorer in the club's history.[[29]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-29) Four days after scoring his first goal, Hazard made his first senior start in a 4–2 defeat on [penalties](Penalty_shootout_(association_football) "Penalty shootout (association football)") to [Montpellier](Montpellier_HSC "Montpellier HSC") in the [Coupe de la Ligue](Coupe_de_la_Ligue "Coupe de la Ligue").[[30]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-30) After featuring as a substitute in the team's next five league matches, on 15 November, Hazard started his first league game against [Saint-Étienne](AS_Saint-%C3%89tienne "AS Saint-Étienne"), and capped the appearance by scoring the opening goal in the club's 3–0 victory.[[31]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-31) His assured performances with the club resulted in Lille offering him a three-year contract extension, which he agreed to on 18 November 2008, tying him to the club until 2012.[[32]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-32)

After featuring as a substitute in December, Hazard returned to the starting lineup in January. In February, he scored the match-winning goal in a league match against Sochaux.[[33]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-33) In the Round of 16 of the Coupe de France, Hazard netted a goal in a 3–2 win over the competition's defending champions [Lyon](Olympique_Lyonnais "Olympique Lyonnais").[[34]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-34) In the final ten league matches of the campaign, Hazard started eight and contributed to the team finishing in fifth place, which resulted in Lille qualifying for the [UEFA Europa League](UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League"). After the season, he was named the [Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year](Ligue_1_Young_Player_of_the_Year "Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year"), becoming the first non-French player to achieve the honour.[[35]](Eden_Hazard#cite_note-young_player-35)
